summary: Backend contract testing for iter-14 long-lived-session + admin deactivate/reactivate. 16/16 pytest cases passed against the preview URL. Verified 365-day refresh_token lifetime on both password login and OTP flows, 15-min access_token, /auth/refresh happy + sad paths (invalid/expired/wrong-type all 401), role-guarded /admin/users/{id}/deactivate + /reactivate with self-guard (400), master-admin-target guard (400), non-admin caller (403), and full lifecycle: deactivate immediately 403s existing access_token on /auth/me AND previously-issued refresh_token on /auth/refresh with detail 'Account deactivated'; reactivate restores both fresh-login AND the OLD refresh_token starts working again. audit_log rows written on both actions. Backwards-compat verified — seeded master admin has no is_active field and still authenticates. Preview DB left clean (1 user, 0 otp_codes).
critical_code_review_comments: GOOD: is_active check in get_current_user uses explicit `is False` — correctly treats missing/None as active for backwards compat.
GOOD: /auth/refresh consistently returns 403 (not 401) with 'Account deactivated' — matches contract and the mobile client's 403 handler.
GOOD: self-guard and master-admin guard both use 400 with human-readable detail, letting the UI show the reason.
GOOD: audit_log rows persisted for both deactivated + reactivated actions with actor id.

OBSERVATION: /auth/login does NOT itself gate on is_active — a deactivated user gets a 200 login response, but the very next /auth/me/refresh 403s. This is safe (session unusable) but slightly wasteful; consider short-circuiting at /auth/login too so mobile doesn't briefly store a doomed token.

OBSERVATION: Two identical /auth/refresh calls within the same second return byte-identical JWTs (exp is in seconds). Not a bug — but if the frontend uses token string equality to detect 'session refreshed', it may false-negative. Prefer using the exp claim or a rotation counter.
test_credentials: admin@cravitoo.com / admin123 (master_admin). Scratch employees are created + deleted inline by the test fixture.
seed_data_creation: None — all scratch users, audit_log rows, and otp_codes created during the run are deleted on fixture teardown. Verified post-run: 1 user (admin), 0 otp_codes.
context_for_next_testing_agent: test_session_persistence.py is a self-contained regression suite for the session-persistence + deactivate/reactivate contract. Run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_session_persistence.py -v`. It uses motor to directly insert scratch users (email domain must NOT be a reserved TLD like .local — use cravitootest.com). JWT_SECRET is read from /app/backend/.env. Preview DB expected to have exactly 1 user (admin@cravitoo.com) before and after the run.
rca of the issue: N/A — all contract items behave as specified.
